title: The Last Weather
premise: Coral Fairweather, a professional translator who has spent thirty years translating everything except her own heart, is hired by the dying Elowen Marsh, last fluent speaker of Kernew, a coastal language that was also the private tongue of Coral's childhood. As Elowen teaches her, Coral realizes the language's final grammar holds the sentence her family has spent decades avoiding—the truth of what happened the summer her mother began forgetting, and who was actually to blame. When Coral's siblings arrive to contest their mother's care, the borrowed words run out: Coral must speak the unsayable aloud in Kernew before Elowen dies and the language, along with the family's careful silence, disappears forever. In the end, the truth fractures the family's old arrangement but leaves something sturdier in its place—a smaller, honest belonging, and Coral as the language's second-to-last speaker, teaching her niece the first words.
about_author: T. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former court interpreter who grew up between two languages and claims to dream in neither. They live near a disappearing coastline and write about the words families refuse to say.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Unsaid
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishes Coral's profession, her meticulous mental ledger of things never spoken to her siblings, and her estrangement from the family home. Emotional beat: competent loneliness; Coral translates for strangers because she cannot translate for herself.

chapters.title: The Advertisement
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She answers an odd classified ad seeking 'a student of patience' and meets Elowen Marsh, a fierce ninety-year-old who tests her with Kernew phrases Coral half-remembers from childhood. Emotional beat: startled recognition, like hearing a dead relative's voice.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. First lessons; Elowen refuses payment, insisting on reciprocity—Coral must answer personal questions in exchange for vocabulary. Emotional beat: unease; Coral realizes the lessons will cost more than time.

chapters.title: What the Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Coral visits her mother, Marguerite, in early-stage dementia, and notices her mother still slips into Kernew lullabies—words she never used with the children. Emotional beat: quiet grief and a first suspicion that the language was a hiding place, not a heritage.

chapters.title: Grammar of Avoidance
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elowen teaches that Kernew has no passive voice—someone must always act. Coral begins mapping her family's old silence onto the grammar. Emotional beat: dawning intellectual excitement shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Counts
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Graham, the eldest, a financial planner managing their mother's care from a spreadsheet. He learns of Coral's visits and resents her sudden reappearance. Emotional beat: his control is revealed as fear; he arranges the family the way he arranges portfolios.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elowen recounts, in Kernew, a summer at a coastal cottage—Coral realizes Elowen was there, was family-adjacent, the summer of 'the accident' the ledger never names. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past is closer than she thought.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Smooths
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Nell, the middle sibling, who keeps peace by never asking questions. She calls Coral, warm and deflecting, warning her not to 'stir Mother up.' Emotional beat: love expressed as containment; Nell's kindness is a kind of power too.

chapters.title: Elowen's Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She discovers Elowen keeps her own inventory—a notebook of every Kernew word she has spoken aloud in the last decade, rationing the language to make it last. Emotional beat: heartbreak; Coral sees her own hoarding of the unsaid mirrored.

chapters.title: The Question Arranged Around
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A lesson stalls when Elowen says the family built itself around one unanswered question, and that Marguerite's memory is the last vault it's kept in. Coral flees the cottage. Emotional beat: panic; the ledger's oldest entry is trembling.

chapters.title: Power of Attorney
chapters.summary: Graham's POV. He moves to place Marguerite in a facility and consolidate decision-making, framing control as care. Coral opposes him; the siblings polarize. Emotional beat: the family's old arrangement hardens into open power struggle.

chapters.title: Intermediate Tense
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Lessons resume; Elowen teaches the tense used for 'was about to say.' Coral practices sentences she has never finished in any language. Emotional beat: tentative courage; the unsaid begins to take grammatical shape.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Briefly Lucid
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, fragmentary. A lucid hour in which she nearly says the thing—names a cottage, a storm, a word for 'blame' that doesn't translate—then dissolves. Emotional beat: devastating nearness; the vault opens a crack.

chapters.title: Nell's Complicity
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Flashback to the summer of the accident: Nell saw something, told no one, and has been smoothing ever since. She realizes Coral is digging. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into defensive anger.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker's Bargain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elowen's health fails; she offers Coral the whole of Kernew—the grammar, the stories, the summer of the accident—if Coral will promise to speak it aloud, not keep it. Emotional beat: the cost of the gift is exactly what Coral fears most.

chapters.title: Graham's Ledger, Balanced
chapters.summary: Graham's POV. He discovers Coral has been recording lessons and accuses her of exploiting their mother's illness for a 'project.' His accusation is projection; he has been managing the family into silence for years. Emotional beat: corruption of care into control, fully visible.

chapters.title: The Storm Word
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elowen, near the end, gives her the account of the accident in Kernew: it was not the mother's fault, as the family arranged everyone to believe, but Graham's—and Marguerite took the blame to keep him from breaking. Emotional beat: the ledger's final entry, written at last.

chapters.title: Convened
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral calls a family meeting at Marguerite's bedside, against Graham's scheduling, with Elowen wheeled in as witness. Emotional beat: trembling resolve; Coral chooses to stop translating and start speaking.

chapters.title: Spoken in Kernew
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. Coral tells the truth aloud, first in Kernew then in English, while Elowen confirms it. Graham's arrangement collapses; Marguerite, in a flicker of clarity, says 'at last.' Emotional beat: rupture and release; the unsaid, said, cannot be unsaid.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Sentence
chapters.summary: Rotating short POVs—Graham, Nell, Marguerite. The family scatters and regroups without its old architecture: Graham's control broken, Nell's smoothing no longer needed, Marguerite lighter even as she fades. Emotional beat: raw, unglamorous honesty as the new normal.

chapters.title: Elowen's Last Word
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elowen dies with Coral at her side, speaking the language to the very end; her final word is Coral's Kernew name, given in the first lesson, meaning 'the one who returns.' Emotional beat: grief braided with inheritance.

chapters.title: The Second-to-Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, resolution. Months later, Coral teaches her young niece the first Kernew words on the same coast, and writes to Graham, who answers in three careful sentences—the most honest he's ever been. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth, small and sufficient; the language lives.
